note: Derived indicators. Read the limitations before quoting any figure.
limitations: Bifurcated and all Kerala villages are whole-village polygons, so population is an upper bound and every percentage-of-area figure is an under-estimate.
39% of the population total is Kerala, where extent is over-stated by roughly 30%.
Protected areas come from the India-WRIS national layer, which republishes MoEFCC boundaries and stops at 2021 notifications; anything notified 2022-24 is missing.
Tiger reserve is the protected-area core only, and is a SUBSET of the protected figure -- never add the two.
Land cover is unreliable below ~25 km2 (NRSC LULC 250K registration error 112-168 m); only 416 of 4,331 villages clear that bar, holding 52% of the area.
Land outside Recorded Forest Area is NOT private land; 346 villages show rfa=0 despite being >50% forest, which are layer gaps.
Mining figures are derelict industrial/mining wasteland (2015-16), not active leases.

Population joins BOTH census directories -- the rural village PCA and the town/ward PCA. 33 gazette entries are urban local bodies (Town Panchayat, Municipal Council, Census Town) and are counted from the town directory. Census Towns keep village-range codes, so a code cannot tell a town from a village.
One village, Valvane in Satara, has no census code in the boundary layer and so has no population figure. "Uninhabited" always means a recorded zero, never a missing value.
